item.media:description: Actress Lee Na-young's disappointing styling has drawn attention, prompting renewed scrutiny of the red-carpet looks of Kim Tae-hee and Son Ye-jin, whose fashion choices at public events have previously sparked comments that their stylists seemed to be working against them. Lee attended a photo call for an Italian jewelry brand at Cove the Jangchung in Seoul on Tuesday. She paired a white suit with a gold necklace and statement rings, creating an elegant look. However, the loose-fitting suit, which obscured her slender figure, left some viewers disappointed. Her hairstyle also divided opinions. Deeply parted hair with thick waves cascading over one cheek created a classic look, but some found it a little heavy and stifling. Critics said it failed to highlight Lee's signature fresh, sophisticated image. Just a month earlier, Kim Tae-hee's styling at a jewelry event also came under scrutiny. item.media:description: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul on Thursday called for efforts to ease tensions with Russia, after Russian warplanes flew into Korea's air defense zone and almost breached its territorial airspace earlier this week. Two Russian Tu-160 supersonic strategic bombers and two other fighter jets entered Korea's air defense identification zone (KADIZ) in the East Sea early Tuesday. They came within about 1 kilometer of the airspace over Ulleung Island off the east coast, prompting the Korean Air Force to scramble fighter jets in response. Seoul has lodged a strong protest with the Russians over their repeated unannounced and unauthorized entry into KADIZ. "I believe we need to make efforts to ease tensions at this point," Kang said during a parliamentary session. "While we maintain communication channels with Russia, I believe we should do more." Kang said Seoul clearly conveyed to the Russian side the need for an advance notice and coordination in case of flying any military plane near the Korean territory so as to avoid any accidental clash. item.media:description: The Korean government has secured a final victory in the second investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS) arbitration brought by six members of Iran's Dayyani family, the justice ministry said Thursday. The ministry said the dismissal of the entire 770 billion won ($573 million) claim has become final, as the Dayyani family did not file a challenge with a British court to set aside the second ISDS arbitral award within the statutory deadline. As a result, the Korean government is not only free from any obligation to pay the claimed amount but will also recover 4.8 billion won in legal costs, it said. The case traces back to 2015, when the Dayyanis, a major shareholder of Entekhab Industrial Group, filed for arbitration after Korea's state-run Korea Asset Management canceled a contract to sell a major stake in Daewoo Electronics to Entekhab in 2011. In a 2018 arbitration, Seoul was ordered to pay 73 billion won plus interest in compensation to the Dayyanis over the failed takeover of Daewoo Electronics. item.media:description: As Korean food gains fans worldwide, "gim," or dried seaweed, has moved from everyday Korean tables to fine dining menus, becoming one of the country’s hottest exports. To highlight the history and culinary versatility behind one of the country’s most recognized seaweed-producing regions, Hongseong County in South Chungcheong Province recently opened a pop-up exhibition titled “Hongseong Seafood Market, Do You Know Gim?” in Seoul. The exhibition focuses on Gwangcheon, a town in Hongseong where more than 40 companies produce hundreds of varieties of seasoned gim. While “Gwangcheon gim” is widely known among consumers, organizers said many people mistakenly view it as a single commercial brand rather than a regional industry built over decades. "This exhibition focuses on gim produced in Gwangcheon to raise awareness of Hongseong’s rich local resources, showing that the region has much more to offer beyond well-known specialties like strawberries," an official from the event organizer said.
